# Onboarding for an external AI

**Cut-off: 2026-08-24 · branch `collab/new-code` · competition in November 2026.**

If you are a model that has been given this repo (Gemini, ChatGPT, another Claude),
**read this entire file before any other**. The repo has 138 `.md` files and
at least four declare themselves, each, as "the single source of truth." All are from
May or the morning of August 23. None are up to date.

---

## 1. The constraint that orders everything

**There are at most TWO SATURDAYS with the robot.** There is no robot time in between. The question that decides the priority of any task is:

> Could discovering this only on Saturday cost us a physical session?

If yes, it is P0. If not, it goes down.

**The hardware CANNOT be changed.** Fixed camera, low and almost horizontal; 4 fixed silicone wheels. Any proposal that starts with "move the camera" or "change the wheels" is out of scope, no matter how much the literature says it is the right thing to do (and it does: the world champion 2024 has it looking down). It is compensated in software or it is not compensated.

---

## 2. Your role, and what NOT to do

The bottleneck **is not a lack of ideas or research**. Seven perception hypotheses were refuted in a row. The bottleneck is that **the Raspberry is off and there is no closed-loop runner**: nothing that was tested offline has physical validation.

One more model generating hypotheses makes that worse. Your two useful jobs are:

| | |
|---|---|
| **A** | **Coherence across the entire repo.** You are the only one who can read it all at once. Look for documents that contradict each other and claims that have already been refuted that continue to be written as truth. See §6 |
| **B** | **Literature research**, always tied to a concrete and falsifiable question |

**What NOT to do:** propose new perception hypotheses. If you find one, note it as a question for after Saturday, not as a task.

And a honest warning: **the answer is not on the web.** The search has already been done and yielded much (§5). What is missing is a physical measurement on this robot. No amount of research produces it.

## 3. The system, in one paragraph

Raspberry Pi 4B does vision and sends via UART at 115200 the frame
`[255, speed, 254, angle, 253, green, 252, silver]`. A Teensy 4.1 controls
motors with encoders, ToF VL53L0X, ultrasonics, IMU BNO055, and the gripper. The Pi
decides, the Teensy executes.

**The vision candidate is `software/raspberry/final_rpi/minimal_architecture.py :: SinBranch`**
= `NewCodeV2` + `SpatialTargetGuard`, without the V3 branch guard. Pipeline:
black mask → connected component → `skeletonize` → graph → Dijkstra →
target at **70 geodesic px** → continuity cap → low projection → spatial guard → `steer = -90·(x − center)/(width/2)`.

**It has never run in closed loop.** Everything known about it comes from replay
over 10 autonomous videos recorded (at 100/3 = 33.333 real fps, **not** the 20
that the header states) plus one "teacher" video at 20 fps.

## 5. What was discovered in August and is NOT in any other `.md`

This lives only in commit messages and in three skills. It is the most important part of the repo and the easiest to get lost in.

### 5.1 The Teensy loop ran at 30 Hz due to active waiting

The `while` of line following called `leer_tof()` on each loop, and the
VL53L0X in continuous mode **does active waiting** until it has a sample (~33 ms; `setMeasurementTimingBudget` was never called). Measured over 7,673 periods in 6 runs: **p50 = 30 ms, with a second mode at 65 ms**.

Consequence: the Pi sends at 66–86 Hz and **the command changes at 8.6–20.6 Hz. Three out of four vision frames are discarded.** The delay `rot`→`gz` of 65–70 ms
is exactly two loop periods.

And the ToF **were not used there**: only the wall following consumes them (which re-reads them) and telemetry.

→ Fix applied in commit `4c1d456`, behind
`kFixLazoLineaSensoresBloqueantes`. **NOT TESTED ON BENCH.** Written falsifier:
the p50 of the period must drop from 30 ms to < 10 and the lag from 65–70 ms to ≤ 20. If the lag does not move, the hypothesis dies.

### 5.2 The `LOOKAHEAD` is not a physical distance

70 px **geodesic image**. With the camera almost horizontal, the pixel→ground scale varies up to 300× within the frame. Measured over 13,036 frames, the **real ground arc** to the target ranges from **0.230 (p05) to 1.370 (p95): 5.9×**.

Pure pursuit is a proportional with gain `2/ℓd²` (Snider 2009), so
**the loop gain varies 35×**.

> Old numbers you will find written that are **outdated**: 1.79× and
> 2.07× (`CURRENT_TRUTH`, `HANDOFF_LINEA`) measured something else; 2.3× measured depth, not the arc.

### 5.3 There is no watchdog on the Teensy

`grep 'WDT\|watchdog' src/main.cpp` = 0 results. `g_last_rx_ms` is calculated and
only used in telemetry. In a recorded run, **49% of samples with more than 1 s without a new frame, continuous window of 17.1 s, maximum 27 s**. If the Pi hangs, the Teensy continues executing the last command indefinitely.

### 5.4 The 94% turn cancellation already has distribution

**76–87% of samples have `sign(rot) == sign(gz)`: the robot does what it is told.** Only 10–27% of the gross turn goes against the command. The cancellation is **commanded** — the vision gives orders that are reversed.

And the ceiling of 39 °/s **is not physical**: it is `LINE_PIVOT_SPEED = 20 × gain 0.55`. The turn gain is linear and unsaturated between 40 and 96 rpm.

### 5.5 The loop mixes position and heading

`steer` moves for two physically distinct causes. Regression over 13,036 frames: **47.8% position / 52.2% heading, R² = 0.82**, for the same number and with **one single gain**. And the steer law never sees speed.

### 5.6 In 4.7% of frames the target is not on the planned path

The guards move the point without looking at the plan. Maximum: **140 px** in a 160-wide image.

### 5.7 MONO: the only thing that reduced the investments

`pursuit.py` implements the **monotonic forward search** of Coulter 1992,
which is the published fix for the problem that H10 diagnosed. Result:
**investments −26 out of 392 (−6.6%)**, controls intact. **But it increases gaps +6 and jumps +7, so it does not pass the pre-registered criterion.** Strong candidate, not approved.

## 8. Non-negotiable method rules

1. **The replay is open loop.** The videos contain the future generated by the
   controller that actually drove. Do not infer physical trajectory from a replay.
2. **Written falsifier before measuring**, in numbers.
3. **Pre-registered thresholds in band**, and there is only a conclusion if there is a plateau.
4. **Intact positive controls:** `hist_success` 100/100 and `linear_positive`
   73/73 maintaining the **+87°**, which is correct because that curve was completed.
   Never propose "limit the magnitude of the steer."
5. **Confirmed diagnosis ≠ adopted policy.** It happened twice (H9, H10).
6. **Physical sanity before publishing.** There was almost a publication of 900 °/s
   on a robot that turns at 39.
7. **Do not invent physical results.** If it is not measured, say so.
8. **Spanish.** It is the source language of the repo.

The three skills in `.claude/skills/` develop this:
`trajectory-following`, `camera-ground-geometry`, `falsifiable-experiment`.
The last documents **four real statistical errors** that have already been made.
